newsitem.title: UK: IOD head says UK needs early interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: IOD head says UK needs early interest rate rise.

text.p: The British economy is in need of a prompt rise in interest rates to keep inflation pressures in check, Tim Melville-Ross, director-general of the Institute of Directors said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television on Friday.

"The economic imperatives right now are for a certain amount of activity to be taken out of the economy, either through an increase in interest rates or through a fiscal package of some kind -- probably both," he said.

The Bank of England signalled this morning that official interest rates were unchanged at 6.0 percent -- its first opportunity to do so since Thursday's monetary meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
Melville-Ross said he expected British interest rates to rise within a month of the May 1 election.

"That may sound like bad news but it's better news than the alternative which is for inflationary pressures which are beginning to emerge in the economy, not withstanding the strength of sterling, to get out of control," he said.
If inflation were to be allowed to rise again, the UK would be back in the stop-go cycle it was supposed to have left five years ago, he said.
